narrative:
The model estimates a 59% chance that you will leave your job, which is why your promotion request has been denied. This prediction is driven primarily by three key factors in your profile.

Your relatively short overall career experience of 1-5 years was the strongest influence pulling the prediction toward leaving. While half of employees predicted to stay also fall in this early-career range, the model sees limited total experience as a notable risk factor for turnover. The second most important factor was that you have not received other job offers while at the company. Surprisingly, this actually pushed the prediction slightly toward staying, as most employees who remain also report no external opportunities.

The third strongest influence was how difficult you found it to get involved in decision-making and share opinions at work. This factor pushed the prediction toward leaving. Compared with employees predicted to stay, far fewer report such low engagement.

Taken together, your early career stage and limited voice in your daily work appear to outweigh the stabilizing effect of not having outside offers, leading the model to conclude you are more likely than not to leave.

The organization should consider giving you clearer channels to contribute ideas and more structured support as you build experience. You may want to discuss these areas with your manager to strengthen your connection to the role.
